neighbours.label: the second word of a fixed compound modifier naming a safety or alerting system or a special football play (emergency alert, two-factor, extra-point, onside, 911), as against the same sentences with a plain noun in its place
fire: Phones across the region buzzed with an amber alert late on Tuesday night.
The bank now requires multi-factor authentication for every login.
Coach chose to go for a two-point conversion instead of kicking.
The city tested its tornado warning sirens at noon on Wednesday.
Their special teams recovered a surprise onside kick in the final minute.
The state launched an emergency alert app for wildfire evacuations.
Most email providers offer two-factor sign-in at no extra cost.
The kicker made the extra-point try after the late touchdown.
quiet: Phones across the region buzzed with holiday greetings late on Tuesday night.
The bank now requires a new password for every account.
Coach chose to go for a long walk instead of watching.
The city tested its new streetlights at noon on Wednesday.
Their marching band played a surprise song in the final minute.
The state launched a tourism app for summer visitors.
Most email providers offer free storage at no extra cost.
The kicker made the team dinner after the late practice.
